claims.text: Adding less than 1 vol.% nanoscale Y2O3 to AlCrFeNiSi powder will mitigate residual thermal stresses in LPBF-built miniature components.
Adding less than 1 vol.% nanoscale Y2O3 to AlCrFeNiSi powder will improve the mechanical properties of LPBF-built miniature components.
Uniform blending before LPBF can produce a uniform dispersion of nanoscale Y2O3 in the AlCrFeNiSi matrix.
The proposed processing window is an LPBF energy density of approximately 100–150 J/mm³ with controlled layer thickness.
The proposed geometry is miniature components with features below 10 mm.
Y2O3 particles act as grain-boundary pinning sites in solidifying AlCrFeNiSi.
Y2O3 particles act as heterogeneous nucleation centers during solidification of AlCrFeNiSi.
The Y2O3 dispersoids produce a refined, equiaxed microstructure.
Heterogeneous nucleation promoted by Y2O3 during rapid solidification leads to finer grains.
Finer grains reduce thermal gradients and residual stresses.
Nanoscale Y2O3 dispersoids impede dislocation movement.
Dispersion strengthening by Y2O3 increases the strength of additively manufactured material.
Y2O3 dispersoids increase ductility relative to unmodified AlCrFeNiSi.
Y2O3-modified AlCrFeNiSi will have lower residual stress than standard LPBF AlCrFeNiSi.
Y2O3-modified AlCrFeNiSi will have finer grains than standard LPBF AlCrFeNiSi.
Y2O3-modified AlCrFeNiSi will have higher tensile strength and ductility than standard LPBF AlCrFeNiSi.
Conventional high-thermal-load LPBF of unmodified AlCrFeNiSi typically produces significant residual stresses and degraded mechanical properties because of coarse microstructures.
The intervention is effective for feature sizes below 10 mm under moderate-energy LPBF conditions.
XRD or hole-drilling can be used to evaluate residual stress in the specimens.
The optimal Y2O3 concentration and required distribution uniformity have not been precisely determined.
